skill.name: nextjs-optimization
skill.description: Optimize Next.js 15 applications for performance, Core Web Vitals, and production readiness using App Router best practices.
skill.summary: Guides Next.js performance audits and improvements for rendering, images, caching, bundles, and Core Web Vitals.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, placeholder URLs, and a nonsecret NODE_ENV example. Two command examples remain confirmed medium-risk because they instruct npm or npx usage, which can execute project scripts or downloaded packages if run without consent.

remediation.issue: Use of npm and npx commands in optimization workflows
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npm run build, npm run start, npx @next/bundle-analyzer, or npx lighthouse.

remediation.issue: Command execution boundaries are not stated clearly
remediation.suggestion: Add a safety note that Bash steps are optional inspection commands and should run only in trusted project workspaces.

static_findings.snippet: - Project uses Next.js (detected by `next` in dependencies)
- [ ] All images use `next/image` with proper dimensions
- Fix: Use dynamic import for `Chart` component
- `quality-gates` - Run build and verify no regressions

finding_verdicts.reason: The dynamic import appears in a documented Next.js code sample for component splitting. It imports a local component path and is not hidden runtime code in the skill.

content.value_statement: Slow Next.js apps hurt user experience and search visibility. This skill guides audits and fixes for rendering, images, caching, bundles, and Core Web Vitals.
actual_capabilities: Identifies rendering improvements for Server Components, static generation, ISR, and dynamic routes.
Guides image, font, and script optimization with Next.js built-in features.
Suggests data fetching, caching, Suspense, and streaming patterns for faster pages.
Provides bundle analysis steps with dynamic imports and tree shaking checks.
Defines a practical report format for issues, fixes, estimated impact, and next steps.
limitations: It does not prove performance gains without real Lighthouse or Web Vitals measurements.
Some command examples require user approval in restricted or untrusted workspaces.
It focuses on App Router patterns and has limited depth for legacy Pages Router apps.
It cannot replace production monitoring after deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Launch Audit
use_cases.description: Review a Next.js app before release and prioritize fixes that affect loading speed and search visibility.

use_cases.title: Improve Core Web Vitals
use_cases.description: Find likely LCP, FID, and CLS issues and map them to concrete Next.js remediation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize App Router Practices
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for rendering, caching, metadata, and bundle decisions across a product team.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Performance Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js app for obvious performance issues. Focus on images, fonts, rendering strategy, and Core Web Vitals risks.

prompt_templates.title: App Router Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my App Router structure. Recommend Server Component, client boundary, caching, and metadata changes that reduce load time.

prompt_templates.title: Bundle Reduction Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Find bundle size problems in this Next.js project. Suggest dynamic imports, tree shaking improvements, and third-party script changes.

prompt_templates.title: Production Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare for deployment with measurable goals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production optimization report for this Next.js 15 app. Include priority, expected impact, verification steps, and rollout risks.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why the home page has poor LCP.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the hero image as the likely LCP element, recommends Next.js Image with priority, and adds verification steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce a large client bundle.
output_examples.output: The output lists heavy client components, recommends dynamic loading for noncritical widgets, and prioritizes changes by user impact.

output_examples.input: A product lead requests a release readiness check.
output_examples.output: The report summarizes current risks, the highest-value fixes, expected performance impact, and a short validation checklist.

best_practices: Measure performance before and after each change with the same environment.
Default to Server Components and keep client components small and interactive.
Prioritize fixes that improve user-visible loading and layout stability.
anti_patterns: Running package scripts or npx tools without user approval in an untrusted project.
Adding use client at high levels when only a small child component needs interactivity.
Treating estimated performance impact as verified results without measurement.

faq.question: Does this skill support Next.js 15?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for Next.js 15 and App Router performance patterns.

faq.question: Can it improve Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: It can identify likely causes and recommend fixes. Real metrics must verify the final result.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it automatically run build commands?
faq.answer: The skill includes command examples. Agents should request approval before running npm or npx commands.

faq.question: Does it handle legacy Pages Router apps?
faq.answer: It can detect legacy structure and suggest migration. Its deepest guidance targets App Router projects.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a prioritized optimization report with issues, fixes, estimated impact, and validation steps.
